messages:
Jordan Lee: hey all — I just posted ADR-0147 (SCM versioning + negotiation) and need reviewers 🙏

Jordan Lee: confluence link: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/ADR-0147+Cost+Model+Versioning+and+Negotiation

Jordan Lee: tl;dr proposal: header-based negotiation (client sends `X-Redwood-SCM-Version` + `X-Redwood-SCM-Min-Version`), server responds with `X-Redwood-SCM-Version-Used`. No version-in-path.

Jordan Lee: would love eyes from platform/api/console/sre/security + docs on the backwards-compat language.

Priya Natarajan: added to my queue. quick q: are we saying “backward compatible within major” or “compatible across all minors forever”? language matters.

Jordan Lee: currently: “SCM v1.x will remain supported for >= 12 months after v2 GA” + “no breaking changes within v1 minor”. But I’m not sure that reads clearly.

Ethan Park: skimmed. I like header negotiation. please tighten the definitions of “breaking” for this API.

Ethan Park: e.g. adding new breakdown components is *non-breaking* for JSON consumers but can be breaking if clients assume sum(breakdown)=total and they hardcode known keys.

Chloe Martin: +1, Console will parse by key. If new components show up we’re fine, but we need to say clients MUST ignore unknown breakdown keys.

Jada Williams: also can we clarify what happens if client requests v2 but only v1 is supported? do we 400 or do we fall back?

Jordan Lee: current draft says: if `X-Redwood-SCM-Version` is unsupported and `X-Redwood-SCM-Min-Version` not provided => 400 `unsupported_version`. if min provided => negotiate highest <= requested and >= min, else 400.

Amara Diallo: I’d strongly prefer we don’t “silent fallback” without telling the client. as long as response includes `X-Redwood-SCM-Version-Used` that’s OK, but Console needs to surface mismatch for debugging.

Chloe Martin: yeah, we can log when version_used != version_requested and attach to request_id. just make it explicit.

Sean Gallagher: SRE angle: 400 vs 200 w/ fallback changes traffic patterns. for canary rollouts, fallback is nice to avoid partial outages. but we need to be super explicit in the headers + audit logs so it’s diagnosable.

Sean Gallagher: also add note that server MAY temporarily pin version to protect SLOs (feature flag / rollback), but must declare it in `Version-Used`.

Naomi Feldman: compliance: avoid promising “forever support” in ADR. 12 months is fine, but add that deprecation timelines may differ for Private/on-prem releases.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: security review note: version negotiation headers are fine, but make sure we don’t let version selection bypass authorization checks (e.g. older versions returning extra fields). ADR should state: authz is version-independent; field-level redaction rules apply across versions.

Jordan Lee: good call — I’ll add explicit “no version grants additional access; redaction policy applies uniformly.”

Elliot Price: docs request: can we standardize header names + examples? Right now there’s `X-Redwood-SCM-Version` and later you mention `X-Redwood-CostModel-Version` in one spot.

Jordan Lee: ah that’s a bug. should all be `X-Redwood-SCM-*`. I’ll fix.

Priya Natarajan: wording suggestion for backwards compat section:
- “Within a major version, fields may be added but will not be removed or change meaning.”
- “Clients MUST ignore unknown fields/components.”
- “Breaking changes require major version bump.”

Priya Natarajan: plus: “Server will always return `version_used` and `assumptions` so clients can display confidence/assumptions consistently.”

Jada Williams: can we also add: “If `min_version` is set, server MUST NOT return a version < min_version” (seems obvious but should be normative).

Amara Diallo: +1. also consider using `Accept-Version` style? but I’m ok w/ `X-Redwood-*` since it’s internal for now.

Jordan Lee: I’ll keep `X-Redwood-*` for v1 and note we can migrate to standards later if we ever expose it externally.

Sean Gallagher: small nit: add error code guidance: `unsupported_version` vs `invalid_request` vs `missing_required_input`. oncall needs crisp distinctions.

Jordan Lee: ack. I’ll update error table.

Chloe Martin: timeline: can we get review by EOD tomorrow? Console integration needs this pinned for the client lib.

Jordan Lee: yep — I’ll incorporate feedback tonight and re-request signoff tomorrow. :thumbsup:

Jordan Lee: action items I’m taking:
- tighten “breaking change” definition + client MUST ignore unknown breakdown keys
- fix header name inconsistency
- add explicit “no silent fallback; always return version_used; log mismatch”
- add security note on authz/redaction consistent across versions
- add deprecation language caveat for Private
- add normative statements around min_version

Priya Natarajan: :white_check_mark: ping me when updated, I’ll re-review.
